Case-insensitive byte searches found no reference to war3map.w3r, war3map.w3c or war3map.w3s in any decoded entry; war3map.imp appears only in lotkt-object-receipt.json build metadata. war3map.w3r (version 7) holds 88 regions, matching the 88 distinct gg_rct_ globals and 91 Rect calls in Lua; war3map.w3c (version 3) holds 1 camera, matching 1 gg_cam_ global and 1 CreateCameraSetup call; war3map.w3s (version 3) holds 7 sounds, matching 7 gg_snd_ globals and 8 CreateSound calls. All 873 war3map.imp rows (version 1) name entries present in the MPQ, so removing the manifest removes no imported payload; Warcraft III reads imported files by MPQ path.
review.limitations: This review applies only to this exact map and script and is an explicit dependency review, not a static proof, complete asset-graph proof or Warcraft III execution validation. The four actual embedded FileIO, MyDataFileLoad, GameResultSaveAdapter and InventoryNativeCompat modules matched the current transformed source bytes; other compiled modules were reviewed as embedded rather than assuming that the whole checkout matches the map. The receipt source-map hash was not matched to an available original map; its source provenance and object adoption were not validated or performed. This does not assert that the current LoTKT.w3x is the build source. External save payloads are assumed to follow the existing FileIO JASS-tooltip data format; modified external scripts, injected runtime code and add-ons are outside the review. Every noncandidate payload and MPQ locale/encryption/attributes/alias contract must remain preserved. Any input or Lua byte change invalidates this contract and requires renewed review unless logically identical repacking is verified by the existing contract-review function. Keep the editable original, history and receipt for World Editor, rebuilding and object adoption. Cleanup applies only to a separately saved distribution/test copy. Actual save loading, gameplay, model appearance, performance and multiplayer synchronization require Warcraft III testing. The editor data candidates are World Editor placement data and the import manifest. Their removal relies on the documented editor-only role of these files and on the matching script definitions above; it was not executed in Warcraft III. Without them World Editor loses regions, cameras, sound definitions and the import list of the distribution copy, so keep the editable original. Test map loading, region events, cameras, sounds and every imported resource in game before distribution.
